correctness.rationale: The unfilled graph hypothesis gives the full t-skeleton plus precisely the (t+2)-subsets with an edge; there are no higher cells. Contraction by augmentation in the exterior chains gives degree-t cycles wedge^(t+1) W, where W is the vertex augmentation lattice. Fixing edge uv, its difference e_v-e_u is one of the integral basis vectors e_a-e_u of W. The boundaries of the top simplices containing uv span exactly (e_v-e_u) wedge wedge^t W. Summing over edges therefore gives the saturated boundary image: the edge-difference subgroup U is the kernel of the canonical surjection W to W_C, and the exterior quotient is wedge^(t+1) W_C. This proves naturality and torsion-freeness, and counting top faces minus boundary rank gives B_(t+1). The t-skeleton collapses after quotienting the contractible star of one vertex to a wedge of t-spheres. For t>=2 the based homotopy classes of attachments from a wedge of t-spheres are classified by the matrix in H_t (Hurewicz); pre- and post-composition with self-equivalences implement the two unimodular changes of basis without changing the homotopy cofiber. Saturation makes every nonzero diagonal a unit, leaving the two types of spheres. This also handles edgeless graphs and the t=n-2 endpoint; for t>=n-1 one can delete to a vertex. The illustrative cycle and two-disjoint-edge ranks agree by direct counting. Inspected verify.py, which tests only finite mod-two ranks; no source checker was executed. The theorem itself is correct; the inaccurate bounded-independence comparison in the source's prior-work section is addressed under originality.
